question: What is the basic medical definition of urinary incontinence?

options.B: An infection in the urinary tract
options.D: The complete inability to produce urine

explanation: Urinary incontinence specifically refers to the accidental or involuntary leaking of urine from the bladder. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is it risky to think of urine leaking as just a normal part of getting older?

options.A: It causes severe skin rashes in all elderly people
options.B: It stops patients from seeking helpful treatment
options.C: It automatically leads to kidney failure
options.D: It means the bladder has completely stopped working

explanation: When patients or their families think leaking is just normal aging, they keep quiet and miss out on treatments that could really help them feel better. Great insight for a nurse! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the primary name of the smooth muscle that forms the wall of the urinary bladder?
explanation: The detrusor muscle makes up the main muscular wall of the bladder and contracts to push urine out during urination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: What must the urinary sphincters do so that normal urination can happen?
explanation: For urine to flow out smoothly, the urinary sphincters need to open up (relax) at the same time the bladder muscle squeezes. Teamwork! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which type of incontinence happens when a person leaks urine while coughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy objects?
explanation: Stress incontinence is triggered by physical movements that suddenly push down on the bladder when pelvic support is weak. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient with severe arthritis cannot walk to the bathroom or manage clothing buttons fast enough, resulting in accidental urine loss. What type of incontinence is this?
explanation: Functional incontinence occurs when the urinary tract is fine, but physical or environmental barriers stop the person from reaching the toilet. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: Which of these is a very common cause of weakened pelvic floor muscles in women?
explanation: The stretching and hard work of vaginal delivery can tire out or stretch the pelvic floor support structures, making leaks more likely later on. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: How do conditions like a stroke often lead to urinary incontinence?

options.A: They cause the kidneys to produce excessive amounts of urine
options.B: They permanently shrink the overall size of the bladder
options.C: They destroy the lining of the urinary tract
options.D: They disrupt nerve signals between the brain and the bladder

explanation: Our brain and spinal cord need to talk to the bladder to control peeing. When a stroke damages those pathways, that communication gets mixed up. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is the main reason for having a patient keep a bladder diary?

options.A: To record fluid intake, leakage episodes, and voiding patterns
options.B: To list all daily medications and food allergies
options.C: To track blood pressure changes throughout the day
options.D: To measure daily weight fluctuations and calorie consumption

explanation: A bladder diary gives you a clear, real-life picture of when the patient drinks, when they leak, and how often they go. Super helpful for planning care! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why do nurses routinely check a urine sample (urinalysis) when evaluating new urine leaks?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To screen for prostate cancer markers
options.D: To measure exact kidney filtration rates

explanation: Infections can irritate the bladder and cause sudden leaks. Ruling out an infection is always a smart first step in nursing assessment. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the common name for exercises designed to strengthen the pelvic floor muscles?
explanation: Kegel exercises involve repeatedly contracting and relaxing the pelvic floor muscles to improve structural support and urinary control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: A patient with urge incontinence is starting a bladder retraining program. What is the right instruction to give them?

options.A: Stop doing pelvic floor exercises completely
options.B: Hold urine for as long as possible until severe pain occurs
options.C: Drink large amounts of water only right before bedtime
options.D: Urinate on a strict schedule, slowly increasing the time between trips

explanation: Bladder retraining uses a set schedule that slowly stretches out the time between bathroom breaks, helping the bladder hold more without sudden spasms. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: Which type of medication is often given to calm down an overactive bladder?
explanation: Anticholinergic drugs block the nerve signals that tell the bladder muscle to squeeze too often. It helps the bladder relax! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is the main goal of sling surgery done for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: To provide physical support under the urethra
options.B: To increase the total urine production rate
options.C: To shrink an enlarged prostate gland
options.D: To relax the overactive detrusor muscle

explanation: A sling creates a tiny hammock of mesh or tissue to lift and support the urethra so it stays shut when abdominal pressure spikes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is a very common skin problem caused by unmanaged urine leaks over time?

options.C: Diffuse bacterial cellulitis of the face

explanation: When urine sits on the skin, it breaks down the natural skin barrier, causing painful redness and irritation called incontinence-associated dermatitis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)

question: Why does ongoing urinary incontinence put a patient at higher risk for urinary tract infections?

options.A: Skin breakdown allows bacteria to travel directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Frequent urination washes away all the normal protective cells
options.C: Moisture and residual urine create an environment where bacteria multiply easily
options.D: Absorbent pads permanently stop the kidneys from filtering waste

explanation: Sticking around in lingering moisture gives bacteria a cozy place to grow and easily find their way into the urinary tract. Good skin care and hygiene prevent this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)
